newsitem.title: CANADA: iStar to finish AT&T Canada deal soon.
newsitem.headline: iStar to finish AT&T Canada deal soon.

text.p: iStar internet inc hopes to complete a deal with AT&T Corp's Canadian unit to offer a chance for homes and businesses to hook up to the Internet soon, said iStar's chief financial officer David Ellis.

"We ought to be able to complete the deal as originally envisaged between AT&T (Canada) Long Distance (Service Co) and ourselves," Ellis told Reuters. The firms were scheduled to offer the distribution service this fall.
"We're optimistic that that's going to get signed and implemented quite soon," Ellis said.
AT&T Canada, formerly called Unitel Communications Co, wants to compete with Bell Canada's service Sympatico. Both Bell and Sympatico are units of BCE Inc.
Ellis also said that, if the right offer came along, iStar management would consider a take-over offer, something that the industry has discussed for a while.
"We've talked for a long time with various players in the United States, but we haven't finalized an arrangement at this stage," Ellis said.
"Over the last year we've received a number of offers, but we haven't got a take-over offer that we've found attractive yet," Ellis said. iStar is based in Ottawa.
Ellis did not rule out talks with AT&T Canada. "We don't reject any offers from any company, but it would depend on all the strategic advantages to us," Ellis said.
